name: Latvian
notes: Latvian (Lettish), Baltic language spoken in Latvia. Palatalised consonants marked with cedilla. Long vowels marked with macron. Three tone system (level, falling, broken).

sources.author: Kalnača, Andra; Lokmane, Ilze
sources.title: Latvian Grammar
sources.notes: The letter-sound correspondence tables (pp. 20-21, prepared by Ilze Auziņa), read in full. They give every letter with an IPA value and an example: the palatals ⟨ģ ķ ļ ņ⟩ = ɟ c ʎ ɲ, ⟨c dz č dž⟩ = ts dz tʃ dʒ, ⟨š ž⟩ = ʃ ʒ, the macron as length, and the diphthongs ⟨ie⟩ = i͜e, ⟨ai au ei ui iu eu ou oi⟩. Three values there that this map should be checked against: ⟨o⟩ is ɔ, ɔː or the diphthong u͜o depending on the word (omārs, opera, ola), ⟨e ē⟩ are e/æ and eː/æː by the same word-level rule (ezis vs ezers), ⟨h⟩ is x and ⟨j⟩ is written ʝ. A reference grammar of morphology and syntax; the phonology is this table and a short section, not a phonological analysis.

stress.notes: Latvian has initial stress in the vast majority of native words. Enclitics and some loanwords may shift stress, but for G2P purposes initial-stress is the reliable default. Long vowels (ā ē ī ū) and circumflex/falling tones (ar̃) mark quantity/tone, not stress position. Source: Nau (1998), Latvian; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_phonology
